title: Assessment
description: What a person means by 'I assessed a tenant': the transferable aggregate. A RunSet alone cannot be handed over because it does not carry what produced it. The canonical half is archived and verified; the derived half is thrown away and rebuilt, and a report that cannot be regenerated from the canonical half is a second original rather than a projection. A diff is deliberately absent: it relates two assessments and belongs to a Comparison.

derived.description: Optional by design. An assessment with nothing derived is complete; an assessment with nothing canonical is not an assessment.

$schema.description: The exact contract this document claims, which must be the $id of the schema validating it. An instance convention and not the dialect keyword: inside a schema document `$schema` names the JSON Schema dialect, and using one field for both meanings is what this separation exists to prevent. It replaces `schema_version`, which was a second version that could not even express the one in the $id — `1.0` against a contract ending in `/1.2.0` — and was maintained by hand.

run_set.description: The evaluation at tenant scale. Referenced rather than restated: the previous version said the structure was owned by the run-set schema and then described an object with one key, so a consumer generated a type that could not hold a real run set.

evidence.description: Every evidence document the run set was evaluated from, whole. A finding whose evidence was discarded cannot be re-checked, and re-checking is the point.

assessment_id.description: Derived from the canonical digest, not assigned. Two exports of the same assessment carry the same id because the same bytes produce it, and an id somebody chose would let two different assessments claim to be one.

tenant.description: Which tenant this describes, read from the evidence rather than supplied. An assessment that does not say is not archivable, because nobody can tell later what it was about; one that says something the documents underneath it contradict is worse, because the digests then prove that contradiction unchanged.

label.description: What a person calls it. Optional, and never used to identify anything.

identity.description: A summary across the evidence, which is a different kind of thing from the identity that observed one document. This field used to hold an identity kind and answer with `mixed`, which is not an identity anybody can authenticate as.

summary.description: `multiple` is never the reassuring answer: part of the archive is tenant-wide and part is one person's view, and the reader resolves that per document rather than by averaging. `not-established` means no document named the identity that produced it.

kinds.description: The distinct identity kinds observed, sorted. Empty only when the summary is `not-established`.

acquisition.description: How the evidence reached the engine, summarised the same way. An archive that mixes collected and imported evidence has one half whose completeness this engine can speak to and one half whose it cannot.

versions.description: What produced this. Without it a finding cannot be explained two releases later, and 'the rule changed' becomes unanswerable.

rules.description: Rule id to the version of that rule as it was evaluated.

collectors.description: Collector name to its version, as the evidence declared it.

hashes.description: What makes the canonical half verifiable after it has travelled. The derived half is deliberately unhashed: it is rebuilt rather than trusted.

algorithm.description: sha256 over the canonical form, which is part of this contract: keys sorted in byte order, no whitespace between tokens, UTF-8 with nothing escaped that does not have to be. A consumer that escapes more, as the ordinary .NET encoder does with apostrophes, computes a different digest for the same document.

canonical_parts.description: Part name to its digest, for every required member of `canonical` except `hashes`. The manifest IS covered, minus its `assessment_id`: that field is the id and the id derives from these digests, so including it would ask the identity to contain itself. Leaving the whole manifest out, which an earlier version did, let `tenant`, `created_at` and `identity_kind` be changed without anything noticing.

canonical_hash.description: One digest over the parts above, in sorted key order. This is what a Comparison references and what `assessment_id` derives from, so two exports of the same assessment agree without comparing their contents.

reports.description: Projections of the canonical half, each saying what rendered it so that the same output can be produced again.

produced_by.description: Which renderer, at which version. A report nobody can regenerate is not derived.

path.description: Where the rendered file sits, relative to the assessment.
